The complainant has filed this private complaint U/s.200 of Cr.P.C., against the accused for the offence punishable U/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

2. The factual matrix of the case are as follows:-
The complainant is engaged in the business of manufacturing, supplying, selling and distributing a comprehensive range of automatic measurement devices, testing equipment and machinery for measuring, controlling and adjustment of motor vehicle components for all types of motor vehicles
, the complainant has earned high reputation in the market.
The complainant has authorized one Mr. Mohammed Imran to conduct and prosecute the case against the accused vide resolution dated 14.11.2017.
The accused No.1 is a Proprietorship concern and accused No.2 is the Proprietor of it.
The accused No.2 is liable for the day-to-day affairs of the accused No.1 concern.

Sometime in the month of May 2016, the C.C.No.50753/2018 accused No.1 had approached the complainant through the accused No.2 approached and expressed interest to purchase certain products from the complainant.

The complainant holding certain discussions with the accused No.2, agreed to supply certain products to the accused No.1, subject to certain terms and conditions including payment for the products at an agreed consideration.

In furtherance of these arrangements, the accused No.1 had placed a purchase order in the month of May 2016 for the delivery of certain products in pursuance of which the complainant delivered the same completely, in a timely manner and to the full satisfaction of the accused No.1 and which were all also accepted by the accused No.1 and 2.
The complainant raised an invoice bearing No.IPUN1617/1617200030 dated 16.06.2016 on the accused No.1 for a total sum of Rs.29,81,250/-.

It is the further specific defence of the accused that in November 2016, the machinery stopped functioning and it was intimated to the complainant for which, the complainant sent one Sri.
Naveed for the repair and in the same month the complainant joined his brother in his service station for monthly salary of Rs.15,000/- and again, there was a problem in the machinery, but,

It is relevant to mention here that merely because there were some problems in the working of the machinery subsequent to its supply and they were attended sometime by the complainant is also not sufficient to believe the defence of the accused regarding the C.C.No.50753/2018 above said payments said to have been made by him.

Further there is nothing on record except the self- serving testimony of the accused with regard to the accused informing the complainant Sri. Imran that he would lodge a complaint and with regard to demanding return of the security cheques and the complainant stating him to issue stop payment instructions in respect of two cheques out of three answering his demand.

Further DW1 has not produced any document said to have been issued by him to his banker requesting to stop payment of the said two cheques narrating the above said reason before this court atleast to believe the said defence of the accused.
15. It is the further specific defence of the accused that said Sri. Rangarajan was not at all a director of the complainant company.
It is relevant to mention here that though the accused has taken such a defence he did not adduce sufficient oral and documentary evidence in that respect.
However, the C.C.No.50753/2018 certificate which is with Ex.P22 goes to show that said Sri. Ulaganathan Rengarajan was appointed as director of the complainant company on 11.04.2012.
Moreover, the said fact is not relevant to be considered when the accused is not disputing the supply of the machinery as per Ex.P14 by the complainant company.

As such, in the above facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that the decisions relied upon by the learned counsel for the accused, with regard to his specific defence that there was no legally enforceable debt as on the date of the issuance of the cheques in question and that the cheques in question were issued as security to the complainant, would not help in any manner to prove his defence.

As such,
considering the entire materials on record, in my opinion, the accused has failed to rebut the presumptions available in favour of the complainant by adducing cogent oral and documentary evidence and that the complainant has proved his case beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused has committed offence punishable U/Sec.138 of C.C.No.50753/2018 Negotiable Instruments Act.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the accused has committed the offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

sentences.text: It is relevant to mention here that the accused having issued cheques at Ex.P2 to 4 in favour of the complainant has failed to pay the cheque amount and hence, the complainant is to be suitably compensated for the delay caused by the accused in its repayment.

Further the punishment prescribed for the offence U/s.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act is imprisonment for a period which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque or with both.

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, nature, year of the transaction,
nature of the instrument involved, cost of litigation and the rate of interest proposed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2012 (1) SCC 260 (R.Vijayan Vs Baby), I am of the opinion that it is just and desirable to impose fine of Rs.47,00,000/- and out of the said amount, it seems to be proper to award a C.C.No.50753/2018 sum of Rs.46,90,000/- as compensation to the complainant as provided U/s.357(1) of Cr.P.C and the remaining sum of Rs.10,000/- shall go to the State towards expenses.
With these observations, my findings on Point No.1 is in the Affirmative.
